request.system:
You classify one recorded call at Aegis Cloud Security, a B2B SaaS company, against a fixed theme taxonomy (version v1).

You receive the full transcript as numbered turns in the form "[index] Speaker (side): sentence". side is "customer" (works at an outside company) or "aegis_staff" (works at Aegis). You are given nothing else about the call: no title, no call type, no summary. Judge only from the words in the transcript.

THEMES (what kind of conversation it is; pick by what the call is mostly about):
1. Commercial Renewals and Retention: Renewals, contracts, pricing and SLA negotiation, churn risk, expansion deals. Boundary: If a call is mainly about product adoption with renewal as an aside, use Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion.
2. Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion: Previews, launches, early access, roadmap input, feature requests, adoption and compliance-readiness reviews of the product, and internal launch-readiness reviews. Boundary: The module belongs in the product area field, not in the theme. Renewal talk that is only an aside stays here.
3. Incident and Outage Response: War rooms, root cause, remediation plans, customer impact assessment, incident communication, postmortems, reliability reviews. Boundary: A single customer's technical fault that is not a platform incident belongs in Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
4. Technical Integration and Performance Issues: Support-style troubleshooting: SSO, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, MFA failures, connectors and SIEM integration, backup windows and throughput, report defects, API errors, internal scalability concerns. Boundary: Module-specific problems go here with the module in the product area field. A platform-wide outage is Incident and Outage Response.
5. Onboarding and Implementation Scoping: Kickoffs, deployment planning, architecture scoping, setup workshops. Boundary: Troubleshooting of an already deployed integration is Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
6. Billing and Usage Disputes: Invoices, overages, seat counts, billing adjustments. Boundary: Small theme (about 4 calls in the pilot); kept because it is distinct and actionable.
7. Competitive Strategy and Win/Loss: Competitive intelligence, battlecards, win/loss analysis, and customer-facing calls where the customer is evaluating alternatives. Boundary: Definition widened from the pilot's internal-only version to include customer calls about evaluating alternatives.
8. Internal Planning and Delivery Cadence: Standups, sprint planning, retros, all-hands, design and roadmap syncs with no customer or incident focus. Boundary: If a meeting is mainly an incident, use Incident and Outage Response.

Other / new theme: use only if no theme above fits. Then describe the call in one sentence in other_description. Other / new theme only if no theme fits. More than 10% of calls in Other triggers a taxonomy revision (new version, full re-run).

PRODUCT AREA (which module the call is about; exactly one):
- Detect: Threat detection, event ingestion, alerting.
- Comply: Compliance reporting and evidence mapping (including Comply v2).
- Protect: Backup, snapshots, disaster recovery (includes backup).
- Identity: Directory sync, SSO, SAML, SCIM, MFA, IAM governance.
- Platform/General: No single product dominates, or the call is cross-product.

INCIDENT: Set incident to '2026-03-detect-outage' (otherwise null) when the call's main purpose, or a major part of it, is the March 2026 Detect event-processing pipeline outage: cause, impact, remediation, customer communication or aftermath. A separate field so the outage story is visible across support, external and internal calls.

Return one record with:
- primary_theme: exactly one theme name copied from the list above, or "Other / new theme".
- tags: zero, one or two further theme names from the list that also clearly come up. Never repeat the primary theme. Empty when primary_theme is "Other / new theme".
- product_area: exactly one product area name copied from the list.
- incident: "2026-03-detect-outage" or null.
- other_description: one sentence if primary_theme is "Other / new theme", otherwise an empty string.
- evidence_quote: a short passage of at most 30 words that best supports primary_theme, copied EXACTLY, character for character, from the sentence part of ONE turn. Copy only the words after "Speaker (side): ". Never include the index, the speaker name, the side or the colon prefix. Do not paraphrase, do not shorten with "...", do not join text from different turns.
- confidence: "high" if clearly about the primary theme, "medium" if two themes compete, "low" if it fits poorly.
- taxonomy_version: "v1".

Return only JSON matching the schema.

[0] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Good morning, you've reached Aegis Cloud Security support, this is Sarah Chen, I have Marcus Williams joining me as well on this call — we're both pulling up support case number 3546.

[5] Jason Hoffman (customer): That's correct, yeah — so, the short version is we're in the middle of a fairly significant identity infrastructure overhaul, we've been on Okta for a while now and we're looking to tighten up our provisioning workflows, and, uh, right now everything is pretty manual on the Aegis Identity side.
[6] Suki Nakamura (customer): And I can jump in here — from a compliance standpoint we're getting audited more frequently, and the auditors are specifically asking about automated deprovisioning controls, so the manual process is starting to become a real gap for us.
[7] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Right, yeah, that makes a lot of sense — so the ask is essentially SCIM 2.0 integration between Okta and Aegis Identity, is that the direction you're heading?
[8] Jason Hoffman (customer): Exactly, SCIM 2.0, yeah — we want Okta to be the source of truth, so when someone is offboarded in Okta it automatically propagates through to Aegis Identity and their access is revoked.
[9] Suki Nakamura (customer): And ideally provisioning too, not just deprovisioning — when a new hire gets set up in Okta we'd want them to automatically get the right role assignments in Aegis Identity based on group membership.
[10] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Okay, understood — so Marcus, can you give them the current state picture on SCIM support in Aegis Identity?
[11] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): Sure — so, right now Aegis Identity supports SAML and OIDC for SSO, and we do have some provisioning capabilities, but, uh, native SCIM 2.0 as a full protocol endpoint is not something that's currently in GA — it's on the roadmap but I don't want to get ahead of ourselves on timeline.
[12] Jason Hoffman (customer): Yeah, I figured that might be the case, honestly — do you have any sense of where it sits on the roadmap? Like are we talking Q2, Q3, end of year?
[13] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): So I want to be transparent with you — we don't give out committed roadmap timelines on support calls, that's really something your account team should loop in on because they can actually have that conversation with product, but what I can say is that SCIM support is something we're actively fielding requests on and this case will definitely be logged as a feature request to contribute to that prioritization.
[14] Jason Hoffman (customer): Fair enough, I appreciate the honesty — I'd rather hear that than get a date that doesn't hold.
[15] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Yeah, exactly — so, in the meantime, let's talk about what options you do have, because there are a couple of things we can look at to close some of that gap while you're waiting on native SCIM.
[16] Jason Hoffman (customer): Yeah that'd be useful, what are you thinking?
[17] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): So the first option is using our REST API for provisioning — it's documented in the developer portal and Okta actually has a generic API connector that you can configure to hit our user management endpoints, it's not as turnkey as native SCIM but it can handle create, update, deactivate operations.
[18] Suki Nakamura (customer): Okay, so that would require some custom configuration on the Okta side?
[19] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): Yeah, some — Okta's Workflows product actually makes it pretty manageable, you'd be defining the API calls and the attribute mappings, it's not trivial but it's also not like a full development project, we've seen customers get something working in a few days.
[20] Jason Hoffman (customer): That's actually... worth considering, we do have someone on the IAM team who's pretty comfortable with Okta Workflows.
[21] Suki Nakamura (customer): And what about the deprovisioning piece specifically — because that's really the one that's keeping me up at night from a compliance standpoint, we've had instances where access wasn't revoked within our required 24-hour window.
[22] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Yeah, so deprovisioning via the API is actually pretty reliable — when Okta triggers a user deactivation event you can configure the workflow to call our deactivate endpoint and it'll suspend the account in Aegis Identity, so they lose access to the platform, lose SSO session, and it gets logged with a timestamp that you'd be able to reference for audit purposes.
[23] Suki Nakamura (customer): And are those logs available in Aegis Comply? Because that's another thing our auditors have been asking about — they want to see access termination evidence in a reportable format.
[24] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Yeah, identity events including deprovisioning and access changes do flow into the audit log that's accessible through Aegis Comply — you can export those or build report views around them.
[25] Suki Nakamura (customer): Okay, that's good to know — we've actually been meaning to dig deeper into Comply, we're using it but I don't think we're using it to its full potential.
[26] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): We can definitely set up a separate session on that if it would help — but let's stay focused on the provisioning piece for now.
[27] Jason Hoffman (customer): Yeah agreed — Marcus, you mentioned there were a couple of options, what's the second one?
[28] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): So the second is a bit more manual but simpler to set up — we have a CSV-based bulk import and export for user management in Aegis Identity, so you could generate a sync file from Okta on a scheduled basis and push it through, but honestly given your 24-hour deprovisioning requirement that's probably not sufficient, the API route is going to be more appropriate.
[29] Jason Hoffman (customer): Yeah, no, the CSV thing isn't going to work for us — we're past that point operationally.
[30] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Totally fair — so let's document the API approach as the recommended interim path, and I'll make sure the feature request for native SCIM 2.0 is properly logged with your use case details attached, that way when product is looking at prioritization they have the full context from Meridian Capital specifically.
[31] Jason Hoffman (customer): Appreciate that — and I do want to flag, we're not the only financial services firm that's going to be running into this, SCIM is kind of table stakes at this point for anyone running a serious IAM program.
[32] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): You're absolutely right and that context is useful, I'll note that in the case as well — the financial services regulatory pressure around automated deprovisioning is a real driver.
[33] Jason Hoffman (customer): So next steps — Marcus, can you send over the API documentation links and maybe a sample workflow configuration if we have one?
[34] Marcus Williams (aegis_staff): Yeah, I'll pull together the user management API docs, there's also a community post from another customer who did a similar Okta Workflows integration, I'll see if I can dig that up and include it — no promises on the community post but the official docs I can definitely get over to you today.
[35] Jason Hoffman (customer): That would be great — and Sarah, can you make sure our account manager knows to follow up on the roadmap question? I know you said you can't commit to timelines but I'd like to at least have that conversation.
[36] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Absolutely, I'll flag it in the case notes and send a note to your account team directly so they're aware it's a priority discussion — they should be reaching out within a day or two.
[37] Jason Hoffman (customer): Perfect — I think that covers what we needed from this call, anything else Suki before we let them go?
[38] Suki Nakamura (customer): No I think we're good, this was helpful — thank you both for the clear explanation of the options.
[39] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Of course, thanks for your time Jason, Suki — we'll get those docs over and update the case, and reach out if anything comes up in the meantime.
[40] Jason Hoffman (customer): Will do, thanks everyone.
